findings.claim: The analysis does not evaluate the node:test/package.json goal at all.
findings.evidence: Goals require: "node:test harness — Arrange-Act-Assert, tests written first; package.json with engines.node >= 22 and test/check scripts". But `gaps_addressed` lists only "lib/platform: atomic write", "lib/platform: lock", "lib/platform: spawn on Windows", "spec backend: locating the openspec CLI", "three-OS CI", and karpathy/OKF log gaps; it contains no node:test, package.json, engines.node, test script, or check script gap. The prior handoff also flagged this exact issue: "node:test runs without package.json".
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit build-vs-adopt analysis and candidate decisions for package.json scripts, engines.node >=22, node:test conventions, and how tests-first evidence will be captured.

findings.claim: The analysis omits the .gitattributes and CRLF-tolerance goal.
findings.evidence: Goals require: ".gitattributes — text=auto eol=lf; parsers tolerate CRLF on input". The `gaps_addressed` array has no `.gitattributes`, EOL, LF, CRLF, or parser-tolerance entry. The prior handoff specifically warned that "CRLF tolerance rests on one untested line in rules/build.mjs and splitFrontmatter rejects CRLF outright," but no candidate evaluates a CRLF parser fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a candidate/pattern for `.gitattributes` and CRLF-tolerant parsing, including explicit assessment of `splitFrontmatter` behavior and tests on CRLF fixtures.

findings.claim: The analysis downgrades the required bounded Windows rename retry into optional work dependent on observing a failure.
findings.evidence: Goals require atomic write with "bounded EPERM/EBUSY retry". The analysis instead says: "The Windows rename retry is unobserved; it is written only after windows-latest shows the failure." `library-candidates.json` repeats this: "The missing 10% is the Windows EPERM/EBUSY-on-rename retry, which is unobserved in this repo and must be observed on windows-latest before it is written."
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the bounded EPERM/EBUSY retry as an explicit phase requirement, while using CI to validate it rather than to decide whether to implement it.

findings.claim: The adopted @fission-ai/openspec dependency lacks a maintenance/version check despite being recommended as a pinned devDependency.
findings.evidence: Candidate cand-009 has `verdict: "adopt"` and says: "A devDependency gives a fixed path ... a pinned version," but unlike other adopted or rejected npm libraries it has no `maintenance` field, no `last_release`, no registry-modified date, and no actual version to pin.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the exact @fission-ai/openspec version to pin and add maintenance evidence comparable to cand-002, cand-005, cand-007, and cand-008.

findings.claim: The analysis does not resolve the prior handoff requirement that lib/platform have a first consumer.
findings.evidence: The assess handoff says: "lib/platform needs a first consumer (rules/build.mjs)." The analysis discusses primitives and says "Both skills and the Karpathy port need the same four primitives," but it never recommends migrating `rules/build.mjs` to consume `lib/platform` or otherwise identifies the first consumer for the new platform module.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a recommendation that `rules/build.mjs` becomes the first consumer of `lib/platform`, or explicitly justify a different first consumer.
